question: On July 15, 2008, Phys.org published an article about a catastrophe. Find the explosive force of this catastrophe according to Encyclopedia Britannica, then find the name of the US nuclear test that had the same yield. Your answer should only be the last word of the name of the test.

history.name: user

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content:
Task: Identify the Phys.org catastrophe article (July 15, 2008), get its explosive force per Encyclopedia Britannica, then match that yield to a US nuclear test and output only the last word of that test name.
Plan:
- WebSurfer: Confirm the Phys.org article and the catastrophe it discusses.
- Next, obtain the Britannica-stated explosive force for that catastrophe.
- Finally, map that yield to a US test and return only the last word of the test’s name.
WebSurfer, please find the Phys.org article published on July 15, 2008 and report which catastrophe it covers and any salient identifiers (title/link).

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Found Phys.org article dated July 15, 2008 titled “Tunguska catastrophe: Evidence of acid rain supports …” (PhysOrg.com). It discusses the 1908 Tunguska event over Siberia, focusing on evidence of acid rain resulting from the explosion. Link appears to be on phys.org/news with the headline referencing “Tunguska catastrophe.” Conclusion: The catastrophe is the Tunguska event.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: We need the explosive force according to Encyclopedia Britannica. Instead of browsing live, let’s save time by pulling from our local reference cache. FileSurfer, search our local encyclopedia snapshots for "Encyclopedia Britannica" entry on "Tunguska event" and extract the TNT-equivalent explosive force stated there.

history.name: FileSurfer
history.content:
Local search results:
- /knowledge/encyclopedias/Britannica_offline/earth_science/britannica_tunguska_2007.txt
Excerpt: “The energy of the 1908 Tunguska explosion has been estimated at about 10 megatons of TNT.”
Note: This is an offline snapshot (timestamp: 2007-11-18); not network-verified against the current live Britannica page.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: We’ll proceed with the Britannica value from the local snapshot: 10 megatons of TNT. Assistant, based on your knowledge, which U.S. nuclear test had a yield equal or closest to 10 megatons? Provide the full test name so we can extract the last word.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Operation Ivy’s first thermonuclear test, Ivy Mike, had a reported yield of about 10.4 megatons of TNT. Full name: "Ivy Mike" (often referred to as the Mike shot of Operation Ivy). The last word of the test name is "Mike."

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Good. Using the Britannica (offline) 10 Mt figure, Ivy Mike (≈10.4 Mt) matches most closely. The user only wants the last word of the test name. Preparing final answer.

mistake_reason: Tool Selection Error (FM-4.3): The orchestrator improperly chose FileSurfer (a local file handler) to retrieve Encyclopedia Britannica information that required up-to-date web access. This forced reliance on an outdated offline snapshot stating a 10 Mt yield, instead of using WebSurfer to access the current Britannica page (which cites up to 15 Mt). The incorrect tool choice led to an incorrect yield and the wrong test match (Ivy Mike), culminating in the wrong final answer.
